pages.title: Coagulative necrosis

concepts.label: Coagulative necrosis
concepts.detail:
I. Coagulative necrosis
➢ The most common type of necrosis
➢ Defined as   death   of cells with preservation of the
  basic structural outlines    of the cells  for days, with
  preservation of the general tissue architecture
➢ Protein denaturation     overcomes enzymatic
  digestion
➢ Seen in most organs after hypoxia/ischemia           except
  brain
concepts.rationale: Explicit source definition, mechanism, comparison, condition or labelled example.

pages.title: Liquefactive necrosis

concepts.label: Liquefactive necrosis
concepts.detail:
II. Liquefactive necrosis
➢   Defined as    necrosis with complete digestion of
    the cells and destruction of the normal
    architecture
➢   Enzymatic digestion overcomes the
    denaturation
➢   Two situations:
   1.  hypoxic/ischemic    injury of the brain
   2.  bacterial/fungal infection, with accumulation of
       WBCs and release of enzymes                           11

pages.title: Fat necrosis

concepts.label: Fat necrosis
concepts.detail:
IV. Fatty necrosis

• Special type of necrosis with focal areas of fat
  destruction
• Seen with acute pancreatitis, due to release of
  enzymes from the injured pancreas
• Grossly:
  fat saponification: visible white chalky areas
• Microscopically:
  shadows of cells with calcification                         17

pages.title: Dry and wet gangrene

concepts.label: Dry and wet gangrene
concepts.detail:
V. Gangrenous necrosis

➢ It is not a distinctive pattern of cell death the
  term is still commonly used in surgical practice.
➢ It refers to ischemic coagulative necrosis         (Dry
  gangrene: frequently of a limb)
➢ When there is superimposed infection with a
  liquefactive component, the lesion is called "wet
  gangrene"

pages.title: Fibrinoid necrosis

concepts.label: Fibrinoid necrosis
concepts.detail: Visual transcription: Fibrinoid necrosis: small blood-vessel injury with fibrin/plasma-protein accumulation. Immune-complex deposition e.g. type III hypersensitivity -> collagen/elastic-fiber fragmentation -> fibrin/plasma-protein leakage. Thick damaged walls contain cellular debris, serum, fibrin; intense red stain. Examples: rheumatoid arthritis, peptic ulcer disease, immune vasculitis/polyarteritis nodosa, vascular reactions (preeclampsia, hypertensive emergency).
concepts.rationale: Explicit source definition, mechanism, comparison, condition or labelled example.
